metadata.title: Autonomous Zero-Trust Identity Orchestration for Edge Computing
metadata.description:
Presentation Topic: Autonomous Zero-Trust Identity Orchestration for Edge Computing.
Description: We are building a self-healing security layer for IoT devices that uses decentralized identifiers (DIDs) and zero-knowledge proofs. It must explain how we eliminate the need for a central authority while maintaining sub-millisecond authentication latency in low-bandwidth environments. Key points: $O(1)$ scalability, hardware-root-of-trust integration, and our "Neural-Guardian" consensus algorithm.
Target Audience: Technical VCs and Senior Security Architects.
Purpose: Investor Pitch.
Slide Count: 15.

editorial-reveal.description: Dramatic staggered reveal for narrative slides

slides.headline: Central Authority Fails IoT Trust
slides.subheadline: Central authority creates a single control-plane failure for IoT devices and edge computing.

slides.headline: Edge Fleets Need Local Identity
slides.subheadline: Technical VCs and senior security architects need identity orchestration for bandwidth-constrained edge fleets.
bullets: Audience - technical VCs and senior security architects evaluating edge security infrastructure.
Demand is framed around IoT device fleets, not unverified market-size claims.

slides.headline: DIDs Move Trust To Devices
slides.subheadline: Self-healing security layer uses decentralized identifiers (DIDs) and zero-knowledge proofs.

slides.headline: Sub-Millisecond ZK Auth At Edge
slides.subheadline: Local proof verification targets sub-millisecond authentication without exposing device secrets.
bullets: Less than 1 ms local checks avoid cloud round trips in low-bandwidth edge sites.

slides.headline: No Central Bottleneck Is The Moat
slides.subheadline: Decentralized identity orchestration outperforms traditional security solutions

slides.headline: Hardware Roots Anchor Device Trust
slides.subheadline: Hardware-root-of-trust anchors DID keys before each edge session.

slides.headline: Neural-Guardian Coordinates Edge Trust
slides.subheadline: Neural-Guardian consensus algorithm coordinates local trust state without a central authority.

slides.headline: ZK Proofs Protect Device Identity
slides.subheadline: Zero-knowledge proofs minimize exposure while self-healing policies quarantine suspicious devices.
bullets: Zero-knowledge proof flows reduce exposed identity data.
Self-healing remediation rotates credentials after anomalous behavior.

slides.headline: No Central Bottleneck Is The Moat
slides.subheadline: Central authority designs add latency, bandwidth dependence, and concentrated trust risk.

slides.headline: Security Architects Need Execution Depth
slides.subheadline: Execution requires cryptography, embedded security, and senior security architect credibility.
bullets: Founder and advisor credentials should come from uploaded team data.
Execution needs cryptography, embedded security, and enterprise security architecture depth.

slides.headline: Capital Funds Proof And Deployment
slides.subheadline: Financial projections should use founder-provided revenue and deployment data before investor use.
bullets: Business model - usage pricing by authenticated device fleet.
Revenue projections should use founder-provided pricing and deployment data before investor use.

slides.headline: Capital Funds Proof And Deployment
slides.subheadline: Investor pitch ask funds proof hardening, hardware integrations, and pilot deployments.
bullets: Business model - usage pricing by authenticated device fleet.
Go-to-market starts with security architects running edge pilots.
Funding ask should be finalized from founder inputs before live investor use.
